articles.title: Current rehabilitation approaches in ALS/MND and use of digital health technology; an international survey of occupational therapists and physiotherapists.
articles.abstract: Occupational Therapists (OTs) and Physiotherapists (PTs) provide rehabilitation at all stages of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)/motor neurone disease (MND), but research is limited on current rehabilitation practice. In particular, little is known about digital health technology use, which is increasingly available in healthcare. This international online survey investigated current rehabilitation practices and digital health technology use among OTs and PTs. A 46-question survey consisting of open- and closed-ended questions targeted OTs and PTs through professional bodies, special interest groups, and social media. Questions explored symptom management, treatment strategies, and digital health technology use in ALS/MND. Quantitative data were analyzed primarily using descriptive statistics, while open-ended questions were qualitatively analyzed using thematic analysis. There were 240 responses from 16 countries (OTs = 85; PTs = 155). Respondents worked in ALS/MND for a median of 8 years (IQR 11). Fatigue (61.3%) and spasticity (45%) were the top symptoms often/always managed by respondents. OTs more frequently managed cognition, with PTs more frequently managing cough and secretions, pain, and prescribed exercise (stretches, strengthening, and aerobic). The majority (89%, n = 213) screened for falls. Only a minority (27%, n = 65) used digital health technology in ALS/MND. This survey investigated the current rehabilitation approaches and digital health technology use among OTs and PTs in ALS/MND. The survey confirmed the diverse and varied roles of OTs and PTs, with overlap in fatigue and spasticity management. Digital health technology use was low among OTs and PTs. These findings can inform future research into rehabilitation practices among OTs and PTs and digital health technologies development in ALS/MND.

articles.title: Lower frequency ECoG features improve longitudinal stability of speech and hand-grasp detection in a patient with progressive ALS.
articles.abstract: Objective. Achieving long-term decoding stability is a critical challenge for chronic intracranial brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). High-gamma (HG) activity from intracranial recordings is the standard signal for BCI control, and lower-frequency features can enhance HG decoding performance. This study evaluated the longitudinal stability of speech and hand-grasp detection models using individual and joint spectral features, and the local motor potential (LMP). Approach. Longitudinal data from a single participant implanted with two 64-channel electrocorticographic arrays were used to evaluate the long-term stability of logistic regression models for speech and hand-grasp detection. Models were trained on individual frequency bands and on the LMP, a time-domain low-frequency feature, and evaluated over 21 months for speech and 13 months for grasp. The best-performing band features were then combined into multi-band models and analyzed for their spatial contributions. Main Results. The LMP yielded the most accurate single feature models in both tasks (speech 93.8%, grasp 99.4%) and showed little or no decline. Multi-band models combining HG with lower frequency bands were substantially more stable than HG-only models and outperformed the LMP models for speech but not grasp. HG accuracy degraded strongly for both tasks (speech:-4.3 percentage points per 100 days, or pp/100 d, grasp:-3.4 pp/100 d). HG+beta for speech showed a negligible decline (0.5 pp/100 d, 95.60.06% overall), and for grasp, delta alone showed remarkable stability (+0.5 pp/100 d), while HG+beta+delta maintained 98.20.09% overall accuracy with flat performance (+0.0 pp/100 d). The advantage of the multi-band models increased over time, reaching +20.6 pp for speech and +10.2 pp for grasp in the last 100 days. Significance. Incorporating lower-frequency neural activity yields more stable long-term speech and grasp detection than HG alone. These findings indicate that lower-frequency and multi-band features may reduce recalibration requirements for simple BCI tasks, and may complement the precision control provided by HG activity. Clinical Trial Information. ClinicalTrials.gov, registration number NCT03567213.

articles.title: Prevalence of C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansions in a Mexican cohort of sporadic and familial amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Objective: Pathological hexanucleotide repeat expansions (HRE) in the C9orf72 gene (≥30 repeats) are one of the most common genetic causes of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in European and North American populations. However, there is limited data on the size and distribution of C9orf72 HRE in admixed populations such as those found in Latin America. In this study, we sought to characterize the role of C9orf72 HRE in a Mexican cohort with ALS. Methods: Peripheral blood samples were obtained from participants of Mexican ancestry attending a multidisciplinary ALS clinic in Northern Mexico ( n = 102) and healthy neurological controls ( n = 75). We performed high-resolution repeat-primed PCR to determine the size and distribution of HRE per allele across both groups. In addition, we used two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests to compare allele-level HRE repeat size distributions between ALS cases, healthy controls and a comparative external dataset. Results: We identified three patients (2.9%) carrying pathological C9orf72 repeat expansions, of which two had a family history of ALS and asymptomatic family members with pathological C9orf72 expansions. Notably, all three patients originated from the same region in Northern Mexico. Kolmogorov-Smirnov testing did not identify statistically significant differences between ALS cases, healthy controls, and a comparative dataset. Conclusions: Our findings suggest that pathological C9orf72 expansions may not be a common genetic variant in this population. Additional studies are needed to confirm this observation, as well as determine whether regional genetic variation may play an important role in genetic risk stratification, particularly in admixed ALS populations.

articles.title: TIP60-mediated acetylation remodels pathological FUS condensates and promotes lysosome-dependent clearance.
articles.abstract: Phase separation and pathological cytoplasmic accumulation of FUS mutants are central features of FUS-associated amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS); yet, the mechanisms that regulate FUS mutant condensate dynamics and efficient clearance remain largely unclear. Here, we identify the lysine acetyltransferase TIP60 as a selective modifier of FUS mutant condensates. TIP60 preferentially associated with FUS R495X mutant condensates and reduced the condensate formation, while having minimal effects on wild-type FUS. TIP60 activation promoted FUS R495X degradation predominantly through the lysosome-dependent pathway. Acetylation proteomics identified FUS K312 as the major site acetylated by TIP60. Acetylation mimicry at K312 suppressed aberrant FUS R495X phase separation, accelerated lysosome-dependent clearance of aggregated FUS R495X, and attenuated FUS R495X-induced cytotoxicity. These findings suggest that TIP60 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy for FUS-associated ALS.

articles.title: Motor neuron disease due to a novel PIK3R1 mutation.
articles.abstract: Mutations in PIK3R1, which encodes the regulatory subunit (p85α) of class I phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K), are associated with immunologic and developmental disorders, but their effects on the nervous system have not been studied. We identified a novel heterozygous frameshift mutation (PIK3R1 c.1710dup) in a patient with common variable immunodeficiency who developed adult-onset, slowly progressive ALS-like motor-neuron disease. Studies of patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) demonstrated PIK3R1 haploinsufficiency with selective AKT activation. Investigation of patient's iPSC-derived motor neurons (iMNs) showed reduced neuronal electrical activity, and markedly increased apoptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed coordinated up-regulation of differentiation and apoptosis programs across neuronal and glial clusters. Engineering the PIK3R1 c.1710dup mutation into healthy-control iPSCs reproduced the impaired electrical activity, increased apoptosis, and transcriptional vulnerability, confirming the variant's cell-intrinsic pathogenicity. In contrast, introduction of canonical APDS2-associated PIK3R1 splice mutations into the same genetic background did not produce these abnormalities, establishing a variant-class-specific mechanism of PI3K dysfunction. Together, these findings define PIK3R1 c.1710dup as a distinct pathogenic variant that links PI3K-pathway dysregulation to human motor-neuron degeneration and expands the mechanistic spectrum of PIK3R1-associated disease.

articles.title: Persistent bilateral STAU1 elevation accompanies increases in p62, GFAP, and phosphorylated tau after traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of long-term neurological disability and increases the risk of neurodegeneration and post-traumatic epileptogenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms responsible for sustained secondary injury and network dysfunction beyond the initial impact remain poorly understood. Staufen-1 (STAU1), an RNA-binding protein that controls mRNA decay, trafficking, and localization to subcellular compartments, is pathologically overabundant in multiple neurodegenerative disease models, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, dementia, and ataxias. Whether STAU1 abundance is altered following moderate controlled cortical impact (CCI), and whether these changes occur alongside increases in p62/SQSTM1, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and phosphorylated tau, remains unknown. Here, using Western blot analyses, we found that STAU1 is persistently elevated in both the ipsilateral hemisphere, including the injury and perilesional regions, and the contralateral cerebrum at 48-h, 1-week, and 1-month post-injury. These increases are accompanied by accumulation of the autophagy adaptor protein p62/SQSTM1, which may suggest changes in p62 synthesis, degradation, or autophagic cargo burden. In parallel, glial fibrillary acidic protein levels as well as phosphorylated tau levels are elevated bilaterally and remain increased 1-month after injury. Together, these findings show a persistent overaccumulation of STAU1 protein levels at several acute time points from 48-h through 1-month after TBI, the first evidence of a previously overlooked factor in the evolving molecular architecture after brain injury. The combination of elevated STAU1, p62, gliosis, and phosphorylated tau in our TBI model provides a basis for future studies on whether STAU1 contributes to injury-associated changes in protein homeostasis and neurological dysfunction, including post-traumatic epilepsy.

articles.title: A step towards modelling amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in primates.
articles.abstract: A new primate model offers a promising first step towards reproducing the spread of ALS pathology across synapses, although important differences from the stereotyped patterns observed in human disease remain to be addressed.

articles.title: BCI-FIT: Feasibility of a customization protocol for communication brain-computer interface systems.
articles.abstract: The BCI Functional Implementation Toolkit (BCI-FIT) is a flexible, user-centered, interdisciplinary customization protocol for non-implantable communication brain-computer interface (cBCI) systems. Here we describe the protocol and present results of a non-experimental exploratory study of the feasibility of this approach and its effects on accuracy, speed, and user experience. Five participants with speech and/or physical impairments resulting from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) completed calibration and copy-spelling tasks with both customized and non-customized versions of a non-implantable cBCI over multiple visits. System customization was adjusted after each visit based on typing performance, participant preferences, clinical observations, brain signal characteristics, and results of simulations and other offline exploration. Three participants demonstrated consistently high typing accuracy under both conditions, with better typing speed and/or user experience under the customized condition. Two participants had low typing accuracy that did not improve with system customization. The subset of parameters modified, and how they were modified, varied widely across participants due to their different needs and preferences. Participants with high typing accuracy reported that system customization led to improvements in comfort, workload, typing performance, and aesthetic appeal. Customization may improve cBCI typing performance and user experience for some individuals with disabilities, but additional investigation is needed. Participant preferences, clinical observations, brain-signal characteristics, simulation results, and typing performance all influenced customization decisions. Additional customization options could support successful cBCI use for a wider range of users.

articles.title: From Reactive Care to Prevention in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Biomarkers, Risk Prediction, and Early Intervention.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) are typically diagnosed only after substantial and irreversible neuronal damage has occurred, at a point when disease-modifying interventions are least likely to be effective. Increasing evidence indicates that the molecular and cellular processes driving neurodegeneration often begin years to decades before clinical onset. This preclinical phase offers an opportunity for early detection, although translating it into clinically effective prevention remains a major challenge. In this review, we examine advances in fluid-based, neuroimaging, genetic, and multi-omics biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, and other NDs. We propose a staged framework, from risk prediction to actionable intervention, to discuss how integrating these biomarkers may improve early diagnosis and risk assessment and guide interventions aimed at delaying or preventing disease onset. Finally, we discuss emerging prevention-oriented clinical trials, the potential and limitations of artificial intelligence-based prediction, and the ethical implications of moving neurological care from reactive management to predictive and preventive medicine.

articles.title: Altered Brain-cerebrospinal Fluid Dynamics and Juxtacortical Microstructural Alterations in Early-stage Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Altered cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics may contribute to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but their relationships with cortical microstructure and functional impairment in patients with early-stage ALS (King's stage 1; ALS-ES) remain unclear. Eighty patients with King's Stage 1 ALS and 82 healthy controls underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), diffusion MRI, and structural MRI. Global blood oxygen level-dependent-cerebrospinal fluid (gBOLD-CSF) coupling was used as a surrogate measure of brain-CSF dynamics. Juxtacortical free-water fraction (FWF) was quantified across 68 cortical regions. Regional clinical associations were assessed using partial correlations, and indirect effects were estimated using 5000-bootstrap mediation analyses. Spatial correlates of FWF alterations were examined using normative neurotransmitter, cellular, mitochondrial, and transcriptomic maps. After covariate adjustment, gBOLD-CSF coupling was significantly weaker and less negative in ALS-ES than in HCs (p FDR < 0.001). Higher FWF was negatively associated with revised amyotrophic lateral sclerosis functional rating scale scores in the left precentral, left rostral middle frontal, left transverse temporal, and right rostral middle frontal regions after Bonferroni correction. Exploratory mediation analyses identified nominal indirect associations in the left precentral and left rostral middle frontal gyri. Regional FWF abnormalities spatially corresponded to serotonin, gamma-aminobutyric acid, mitochondrial, neuronal, endothelial, and immune-related normative maps. ALS-ES is characterized by altered brain-CSF coupling and spatially patterned juxtacortical extracellular-water abnormalities associated with functional impairment. Normative molecular mapping nominates neurovascular, neuronal, and immune-related contexts for this imaging phenotype.

articles.title: Brain variation underlying genetic factors linked to psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
articles.abstract: Psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions have both shared and distinct symptomatology, but the brain mechanisms underlying diagnostic similarities and differences remain unclear. Using genome-wide association data, we analyzed 12 psychiatric disorders and four neurodegenerative diseases, assessing polygenic overlap, shared loci, and genetic causal relationships linking their genetic latent factors with 3,935 brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDP). Using genomic structural equation modeling, we identified an internalizing factor (F1), an addiction factor (F2), a factor related to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (F3), a neurodevelopmental factor (F4), and a factor related to Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (F5). These showed shared transcriptomic enrichments for frontal and anterior cingulate cortical regions, while F1-specific depletion in substantia nigra and F3-specific enrichment in nucleus accumbens appeared to be specific. Fine-mapping identified 99 variants, including shared loci (e.g., VRK2: F1, F2, F3; TSHZ3: F1, F2; TCF4: F1, F3) and factor-specific loci (e.g., DRD2-F2; SCN2A-F3; FOXP2-F4; TNIP1-F5). The brain-wide analysis of fine-mapped loci identified 1,480 IDP associations (false discovery rate q<0.05). Among these, BANK1 rs1813006, related to F2, was associated to >400 brain IDPs (mostly related to cortical area, cortical grey-white contrast, cortical thickness, and regional and tissue volume). Similarly, MOBP rs1768190 related to F5 was associated with >200 brain IDPs, with about half of them related to cortical thickness. The present study provides new insights into cross-diagnostic mechanisms linking genetic variation and molecular changes to the brain structural and functional variation across psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions.
articles.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

articles.title: Lived experiences of fatigue in individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: a qualitative study.
articles.abstract: Fatigue is a prominent and burdensome symptom of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Its measurement is difficult due to limited definition of the characteristics of fatigue unique to ALS. We aimedto characterize the lived experience of fatigue in ALS, including how it is perceived, understood and experienced, to inform a disease-specific, patient-centred conceptual framework. We developed an interview guide based on existing fatigue scales, review of the literature on fatigue in ALS and the experiences of ALS care providers. We conducted focus groups of people with ALS with open-ended discussion of the fatigue experience. Thematic analysis with a phenomenological approach was employed to identify primary themes. Four focus groups were held with a total of fifteen participants. People reported that fatigue shaped their daily activity and sleep patterns, was worsened by activity and improved with rest, changed social interactions, incorporated mental, physical and emotional components, and was manageable with various means of physical and psychological coping. Some participants reported difficulty distinguishing between physical weakness from ALS and physical fatigue. We identified four interconnected themes that illuminate how fatigue is experienced, interpreted, and given meaning in the everyday lives of people with ALS, extending beyond traditional clinical characterizations. This work has informed development of a conceptual model and a preliminary patient-informed definition of fatigue in ALS. Participants defined fatigue as an all-encompassing phenomenon that feels unique to ALS, is related to weakness, and has physical and mental components only partially managed through rest, expectation-setting and activity modulation.

articles.title: MultiNSDE: treatment-aware neural SDEs for generative modeling of real and counterfactual patient trajectories.
articles.abstract: Synthetic patient data may facilitate biomedical research, trial planning, and the construction of synthetic control arms, but there is a lack of methods that enable the realistic generation of mixed-type longitudinal clinical trial data while accounting for treatment effects. We developed MultiNSDE, a neural stochastic differential equation framework for modeling high-dimensional static and longitudinal clinical study data, including continuous, categorical, and time-to-event outcomes. The model separates treatment- and placebo-associated dynamics, enabling treatment-aware individual trajectory simulation and counterfactual treatment assignment. MultiNSDE was evaluated on three neurodegenerative disease trial datasets: A4 in Alzheimer's disease, PRO-ACT in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and DATATOP in Parkinson's disease. The model reproduced static and longitudinal data distributions, extrapolated clinically plausible trajectories, and generated coherent counterfactual outcomes under treatment-to-placebo and placebo-to-treatment shifts. Synthetic data generated by MultiNSDE preserved average treatment effect estimates observed in the real datasets. MultiNSDE provides a proof-of-concept for the generation of realistic mixed-type longitudinal clinical trial data while preserving clinically meaningful treatment-associated differences in outcomes. It may support disease modeling, counterfactual simulation, and synthetic control generation in neurodegenerative disease research.
authors: Pooled Resource Open-Access ALS Clinical Trials

articles.title: Safety, tolerability, and effect of nusinersen in ambulatory and non-ambulatory adults with 5q-SMA treated up to five years.
articles.abstract: BackgroundNusinersen treatment of adults with 5q-SMA was found to be safe and stabilizes or improves motor function in the short-term (<38 months), but data examining longer-term (>38 months) impact and safety is lacking.ObjectiveTo study the long-term (24-60 months) effects and safety profile of nusinersen in adults with 5q-SMA.MethodsWe conducted a observational study of 5q-SMA patients, age ≥18 years, and receiving nusinersen for ≥24 months. Data were analyzed by ambulatory status. Clinical outcomes included: 6-minute walk test (6MWT), Hammersmith Functional Motor Scale - Expanded (HFMSE) scores, revised upper limb module (RULM) scores, pulmonary function test results, and medication-related adverse effects. Data were collected at baseline and post-treatment initiation at months 2, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 +/- 2 months. Linear mixed models with random intercept for each patient were used to examine the changes of outcomes across time.ResultsThiry-two individuals with 5q-SMA (17 female) were included. Nineteen were non-ambulatory (mean age 38.3+/- 12.1 years) and 13 were ambulatory (mean age 32.9+/-9.5 years) at treatment onset. Average treatment duration was 53.3 months (range 24-60 months). The ambulatory group showed stability in 6MWT and HFMSE compared to baseline. In non-ambulatory patients, RULM and FVC remained stable. No serious adverse events attributable to nusinersen were reported.ConclusionsLong-term nusinersen treatment is safe in adults with SMA. Patients showed relative clinical stability over 60 months. These findings suggest that nusinersen may provide relative improvement compared to the natural disease progression over 2-5 years of treatment.

articles.title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Preceded by Vocal Fold Atrophy.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects the upper and lower motor neurons of the brain and spinal cord, ultimately leading to respiratory failure. Vocal fold atrophy (VFA) is characterized by vocal fold arch atrophy, prominent vocal processes, and a spindle-shaped glottis gap. We herein report an 81-year-old male patient diagnosed with ALS shortly after VFA onset. VFA is generally associated with aging and Parkinson's disease; however, our report indicates that dysphonia may precede bulbar symptoms, and VFA is a suggestive sign in an atypical ALS diagnosis.

articles.title: Evaluation of glucosamine coated mesoporous silica nanoparticles for antioxidant activity cytocompatibility and blood brain barrier permeability in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) remains a fatal neurodegenerative disease with limited disease-modifying options, and effective delivery of therapeutics to the central nervous system is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Here, we report mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) designed as a combination-delivery platform integrating riluzole, 5-methoxytryptamine (5MT) as an antioxidant-related component, and glucosamine as a biomolecular surface coating. The resulting multifunctional nanosystems were prepared and characterized by complementary physicochemical techniques, supporting successful incorporation of the selected components within the MSN-based carrier. To obtain a first-pass indication of brain-oriented delivery feasibility, permeability was assessed using a PAMPA-BBB assay that mimics key features of the brain lipid environment. This screening assay showed formulation-dependent apparent silica carryover across the artificial lipid membrane and provides a basis for subsequent evaluation in cell-based BBB models, supporting their further evaluation as ALS-oriented nanodelivery candidates. Overall, these results establish a rational proof-of concept of MSN platform for combination delivery and provide a permeability-screening basis for subsequent studies in more advanced BBB and neurobiological models, supporting their further evaluation as multifunctional delivery platforms for neurodegenerative diseases, such as ALS.

articles.title: Integrative spatial metallomics: a tutorial review of multimodal elemental imaging workflows, challenges and opportunities.
articles.abstract: Spatially resolved molecular assays are increasingly used to study human health and disease, revealing complex tissue organization beyond what is accessible through bulk analyses. While spatial transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic approaches have rapidly matured, quantitative mapping of metals and trace elements in biological tissues and biominerals through elemental imaging remains comparatively nascent. Elemental distributions alone often provide limited biological interpretation without contextualization within the tissue microenvironment. Here, we summarize themes and computational strategies for integrating spatial elemental data with histopathology and complementary spatial molecular assays. We highlight multimodal approaches for tissue alignment, pixel-wise clustering, and correlative analysis, illustrated through limited use cases involving amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and kidney stone formation. In the ALS cohort, pixel-level elemental profiles were clustered and compared with annotated tissue structures. In the kidney stone cohort, spatial gradients and correlations in elemental and biomolecular features from the renal papilla through the medulla to cortex were examined. Finally, we discuss key challenges for cross-sample, cohort-level analyses, including differences in spatial resolution, normalization, tissue architecture, and mechanistic inference. Addressing these challenges will require interdisciplinary collaboration, enhanced biobanking practices, and development of computational and statistical frameworks.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

articles.title: Liposomal delivery of a riluzole-butyric acid mutual prodrug enhances neuroprotection and cognitive recovery in experimental Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterised by cognitive decline, impaired synaptic signalling and persistent neuroinflammation. Current therapies primarily provide symptomatic relief and have limited effects on disease progression. Riluzole, approved for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, exhibits neuroprotective effects through modulation of glutamatergic signalling, but its poor oral bioavailability limits its therapeutic potential. Butyric acid, a short-chain fatty acid postbiotic produced by gut microbial fermentation, possesses well-established anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. In this study, a mutual prodrug of riluzole and butyric acid was synthesised and encapsulated into liposomes to investigate its effects on drug distribution and preclinical efficacy. The prodrug-loaded liposomes exhibited an average particle size of 322 nm, zeta potential of -7.95 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 43.49%. Oral administration significantly improved cognitive performance and attenuated neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in an AlCl 3 -induced AD-like rat model. Administration of prodrug-loaded liposomes led to the highest concentrations of riluzole in brain homogenates among the relevant treatment groups. Overall, the prodrug-loaded liposomes demonstrated better therapeutic efficacy than the prodrug suspension, individual drug-loaded liposomes and their respective conventional formulations. The enhanced therapeutic performance is attributed to the complementary pharmacological actions of riluzole and butyric acid, combined with the ability of the liposomal system to improve drug bioavailability and facilitate cerebral delivery.

articles.title: Novel VAPB variants in sporadic ALS promote protein aggregation and PERK-ISR associated apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated protein B (VAPB) has been established as a causative gene for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, VAPB mutations have been infrequently reported, and the pathogenic mechanisms underlying novel variants remain poorly characterized. In the present study, VAPB was sequenced in a cohort of Chinese patients with sporadic ALS to identify novel variants and delineate their functional consequences. Targeted next-generation sequencing was conducted in non-consecutive ALS patients referred to Departments of Neurology at Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between 2017 and 2024. Variant pathogenicity was assessed using PolyPhen-2, MutationTaster, and other in silico prediction tools. Functional analyses comprised immunofluorescence, solubility fractionation, immunoblotting for PERK, eIF2α, and ATF4, and Annexin V-APC/7-AAD flow cytometry. Three novel heterozygous missense variants, c.38 A > C (p.Q13P), c.511G > A (p.E171K), c.659 T > G (p.L220R), and one known c.166C > T (p.P56S) mutation, were individually identified in four patients with sporadic ALS. All patients showed relatively rapid disease progression except the patient with P56S mutation. Most in silico prediction tools classified Q13P and E171K as likely damaging. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated that Q13P and E171K, but not L220R, formed perinuclear aggregates showing extensive colocalization with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone PDI. In Neuro-2a cells, upon tunicamycin treatment, overexpression of Q13P or E171K was associated with increased p-PERK/PERK and p-eIF2α/eIF2α ratios and elevated ATF4 expression. Furthermore, independent of tunicamycin treatment, these mutants suppressed global protein synthesis, as assessed by the SUnSET assay. Furthermore, both variants increased the protein levels of CHOP, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3 and were associated with an increased proportion of Annexin V-positive cells. Our findings demonstrate that the VAPB variants Q13P (MSP domain) and E171K (coiled-coil domain), but not L220R, are associated with ER aggregates and converge on activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 branch of the integrated stress response (ISR), accompanied by ER stress-associated apoptosis (increased CHOP, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3). These observations are consistent with a likely pathogenic role for these two variants and indicate that variants arising in distinct structural domains converge on a shared ER stress-PERK-ISR-apoptosis axis, a candidate therapeutic target in VAPB-associated ALS.

articles.title: Takotsubo Syndrome in Acute and Chronic Neurological Conditions: A Systematic Review of Cardiac Phenotypes and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute, usually reversible form of left ventricular dysfunction that mimics acute coronary syndrome and carries a long-term prognosis comparable to that of myocardial infarction. Its pathogenesis has been linked to the brain-heart axis, and TTS has been described after acute neurological events and in patients with chronic neurological disease. However, the evidence remains fragmented across individual conditions, and acute triggers are rarely distinguished from pre-existing disorders. The objective here is to systematically review primary observational evidence on TTS in adults with acute and chronic neurological conditions, with emphasis on the temporal relationship, cardiac phenotypes, complications, and clinical outcomes, and to summarize the mechanistic evidence reported by the included studies. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and ResearchGate (January 2016 to September 2026) in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, supplemented by citation searching. Eligibility criteria, data extraction, and quality appraisal with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were predefined. Of 3170 records, 16 primary observational studies were included: five multicenter registry analyses, four administrative database analyses, five cohort studies, one case-control study, and one cross-sectional study. Reviews and case reports provided context only, and reports from overlapping data sources were not pooled. In the International Takotsubo Registry, an acute neurological disorder preceded TTS in 6.7% of 2402 patients, most often seizures, intracranial hemorrhage, or cerebral ischemia, and TTS was diagnosed within two days of neurological symptoms in 87.3%. In the German-Italian-Spanish Takotsubo Registry, 17% of 2301 patients had a neurological disorder, mostly pre-existing. Neurologically associated TTS showed lower left ventricular ejection fraction (37.4% vs 41.0%), more cardiogenic shock (15.1% vs 8.6%), and higher in-hospital mortality (17.4% vs 4.0%; adjusted odds ratio 3.20), which reached 30.4% after intracranial hemorrhage. A neurological disorder independently predicted long-term mortality (hazard ratio 1.72). Migraine was associated with lower adjusted mortality, whereas amyotrophic lateral sclerosis was associated with a more severe in-hospital course. Ballooning patterns differed only modestly, and chest pain was reported in 29.0% of neurologically associated cases compared with 72.9% of other cases. Evidence for traumatic brain injury was limited to one strain-defined cohort and coded trauma data, and direct mechanistic measurements were scarce. Neurological disease identifies a higher-risk subgroup of patients with TTS who often present without chest pain. TTS should be considered in patients with acute neurological events who develop unexplained hemodynamic instability, electrocardiographic changes, or troponin elevation, and echocardiography should anticipate more severe systolic dysfunction. The evidence base is small, partly overlapping, and diagnostically heterogeneous, and outcomes were reported as all-cause. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic criteria and separate reporting of cardiac and neurological outcomes are needed.

articles.title: All Roads Lead to Rome: Non-canonical Modulators of RNA Metabolism in ALS Pathogenesis.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive motor neuron loss. Aberrant RNA metabolism is one of its most consistent molecular features, and ALS has long been framed as a disease of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), given that mutations in RBPs are among the most frequent genetic causes of ALS. However, a growing number of ALS-associated genes encode proteins that lack canonical RNA-binding domains; nonetheless, their mutations also disrupt RNA homeostasis. This review examines how these non-canonical disease modulators perturb RNA metabolism. We group these factors into three functional classes. One includes proteostasis regulators, whose dysfunction impairs protein quality control and promotes the accumulation of aggregation-prone RBPs in cytoplasmic inclusions and persistent stress granules. Another involves factors that elicit RNA toxicity or disrupt ribonucleoprotein organization, including GGGGCC repeat expansion in C9ORF72 and CAG repeat expansion in ATXN1. The third class comprises factors governing axonal RNA granule transport. Across these categories, a shared consequence is the disruption of mRNA processing, stability, localization, and translation in motor neurons. We further discuss how epitranscriptomic dysregulation, particularly altered m6A and m1A modification states, may contribute to ALS pathology. We also discuss the therapeutic implications of this mechanistic convergence in defective RNA metabolism in ALS.

articles.title: Increased resting muscle activity in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Increased muscle activity during intended rest is frequently observed in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but its clinical significance remains unclear. Our aim was to compare resting muscle activity during transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) between ALS patients and patient controls, and to correlate it with clinical and neurophysiological parameters. Resting muscle activity was assessed retrospectively by counting the number of stimulation attempts in a standardized paired-pulse TMS protocol that were rejected by the software. Stimulations were rejected if the resting electromyography (EMG) signal exceeded 30 µV at least five times during the 300 ms before the TMS stimulus. Secondary outcomes included the revised ALS functional rating score (ALSFRS-R), the revised upper motor neuron (UMN) score, the muscle strength (MRC) score, TMS, and quantitative EMG (qEMG) parameters. Seventy ALS patients aged 68.4 ± 10.3 years (mean ± SD) were compared with 73 patient controls (63.8 ± 13.8 years). ALS patients had significantly more rejected stimulations due to preceding EMG activity than patient controls (adjusted estimates 27.28 vs 7.28, p = 4.13 × 10^-7). Among ALS patients, those with UMN signs had more rejected stimulations than those without UMN signs (medians 40 vs 20, p = 0.025). The number of rejected stimulations correlated with fasciculation potentials (FPs) (rho = 0.3, p = 0.020) and two clinical markers of UMN dysfunction, including brisk jaw jerk (rho = 0.26, p = 0.032) and biceps reflexes (rho = 0.25, p=0.038). Compared with patient controls, ALS patients exhibited increased resting muscle activity during TMS examination. These findings may provide further insight into the pathophysiology of ALS.

articles.title: Optimized gGBE enables robust G-to-Y conversion in mammalian cells and zebrafish embryos.
articles.abstract: Base editing is a powerful and precise genome-editing tool capable of introducing single-base substitutions with high resolution. Depending on the base-modification domains employed, base editors can mediate both transition and transversion base editing in mammalian cells. While deaminase-derived base editors have enabled efficient transition editing in the zebrafish genome, glycosidase-derived transversion editing remains a significant challenge. In this study, guided by structural insights into the Cas9 complex, we engineered a series of glycosidase guanine base editor (gGBE) constructs by inlaying the N-methylpurine DNA glycosylase (MPG) domain into Cas9 protein. Among these variants, we identified a high-performance gGBE in which MPG was inserted between residues G1246 and S1247 of the PI domain in Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, which we named gGBE-PIGS. This variant improved editing efficiency by up to 3.5-fold in mammalian cells and 13-fold in zebrafish embryos, without compromising editing precision. Furthermore, we developed a gGBE-editing-responsive GFP reporter to monitor editing efficiency and enrich for gGBE-edited cells and embryos. Using a combination of the optimized gGBE-PIGS and the GFP reporter, we successfully generated zebrafish models carrying mutations homologous to human amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated variants. Together, these findings highlight the robustness and versatility of the gGBE platform for precise base editing and underscore its promising potential for in vivo disease modeling and therapeutic genome engineering. 碱基编辑是一种高效且精准的基因组编辑工具，可实现高分辨率单碱基替换。根据所采用的碱基修饰结构域不同，碱基编辑器在哺乳动物细胞中既可介导转换型编辑，也可实现颠换型编辑。尽管基于脱氨酶的碱基编辑器已在斑马鱼基因组中实现高效转换编辑，但基于糖基化酶的颠换编辑仍然面临较大挑战。该研究基于 Cas9 复合体的结构信息，将 N-甲基嘌呤 DNA 糖基化酶结构域（MPG）嵌入 Cas9 蛋白内部，构建了一系列糖基化酶型鸟嘌呤碱基编辑器（gGBE）。研究发现将MPG插入到化脓性链球菌Cas9（SpCas9）PI结构域的G1246与S1247残基得到的gGBE-PIGS总体编辑效率最高。相比N-端融合的gGBE，gGBE-PIGS在哺乳动物细胞中的编辑效率最高可提升 3.5 倍，在斑马鱼胚胎中最高可提升 13 倍，且编辑精确度未受影响。此外，该研究构建了gGBE 编辑响应型 GFP 报告系统，该系统可用于监测编辑效率，同时富集经 gGBE 编辑的细胞和胚胎。结合优化后的 gGBE-PIGS 与 该GFP 报告系统，该研究成功构建了携带人类肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）同源突变的斑马鱼疾病模型。综上所述，该研究证明了gGBE在精准碱基编辑领域的高效性与多样性，并揭示其在体内疾病模型构建及基因治疗领域的潜在应用前景。.

articles.title: Parietal GABA in individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and asymptomatic C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers assessed with MR spectroscopy at 7 T.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease. Multiple pathways are involved in its pathophysiology, but the exact mechanisms are still unknown. In this study, we investigate the role of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in ALS and the related C9orf72 repeat expansion (C9). As the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, GABA may affect hyperexcitability in ALS. Decreased GABA levels have been reported in the motor cortex in ALS, but neither regions outside the motor area nor carriers of ALS-related pathogenic genetic variants were investigated. We used GABA-edited magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MEGA-sLASER) at 7 T to examine ratios of GABA to creatine. We compared individuals with ALS ( n = 17) to controls ( n = 13) and separately compare asymptomatic C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers ( n = 5) to non-carriers ( n = 7) from a single family. We placed the voxel of interest in the parietal lobe as it is specifically at risk in C9 carriers. We found no statistically significant differences in mean GABA ratios in either comparison, but individuals with ALS showed a higher variance than controls ( p = 0.026). We conclude that parietal GABA is not involved in ALS pathology in all individuals with ALS, but increased variance indicates heterogeneity and may reflect subgroups with GABAergic dysfunction. Individuals with ALS have an increased variance in parietal GABA levels compared to healthy controls.GABA levels in the parietal lobe do not significantly differ between controls and individuals with ALS.GABA levels in the parietal lobe are not affected by the C9orf72 repeat expansion in the parietal lobe.

articles.title: Context matters: serum neurofilament light chain, a diagnostic aid in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
Developmental and age-acquired somatic mutations in neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: Classical genetic studies have assumed a uniform genome across the body, but humans are genetic mosaics harboring distinct somatic mutations acquired during development and aging. The role of somatic mosaicism in neurodegenerative disease remains poorly understood. In this article, we review somatic mosaicism in two contexts: developmental mosaics arising during embryogenesis and age-associated clonal expansions. Developmental mosaics are established contributors to neurodevelopmental disorders, with emerging evidence linking them to adult-onset neurodegeneration, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and Alzheimer's disease. Postnatal clonal expansions in microglia and hematopoietic cells may further promote systemic inflammation and disease progression. We synthesize these findings into a framework in which developmental and age-acquired mutations contribute to neuronal vulnerability, disease heterogeneity, and the pathogenesis of sporadic neurodegenerative disorders.

articles.title: Dual augmentation of STMN2 and GRN delays disease progression through coordinated axonal and neuroimmune support in ALS models.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder primarily driven by TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) proteinopathy, which triggers early axonal disintegration and disrupts central nervous system homeostasis. Current therapeutic options remain limited. To address these core pathologies, we developed a dual-gene therapeutic strategy that simultaneously restores two pivotal factors: progranulin (GRN), a multifunctional effector critical for lysosomal function and neuroinflammation regulation, and stathmin-2 (STMN2), an essential regulator of axonal integrity and regeneration whose loss is directly linked to TDP-43 pathology. In TDP-43 A315T transgenic mice, this combined therapy significantly extended survival, preserved motor performance, and maintained neuromuscular integrity. In human iPSC-derived motor neurons, the dual therapy promoted axonal regeneration following injury. Mechanistically, treatment coordinately restored axonal and synaptic gene programs in motor neurons while upregulating lysosomal pathways in microglia and neuronal support genes in astrocytes, collectively rebalancing neuronal and glial function. These findings establish that dual augmentation of GRN and STMN2 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for ALS.

articles.title: Long-term stability of cellular-resolution brain-computer interface recordings after stroke.
articles.abstract: Implantable brain-computer interfaces (iBCIs) with single-neuron resolution are showing great promise for restoring mobility and communication in individuals with spinal cord injury or motor neuron disease. Stroke is the most common cause of acquired brain injury and a major contributor to long-term disability, making chronic stroke a highly relevant indication for iBCIs. However, whether stable intracortical recordings can be obtained from the structurally lesioned human brain is unknown. Approach: We report recordings from four 64-channel microelectrode arrays implanted in a participant with chronic aphasia after a large left-hemispheric stroke. The arrays targeted right-hemispheric frontoparietal regions homotopic to the damaged left-hemispheric language network.Main results: Across 111 sessions spanning 1,240 days, unit yield and signal quality remained stable. Waveform-based tracking reliably identified individual units across sessions, including across extended recording gaps. Short- and long-term unit stability was comparable to previous reports from iBCI participants without structural brain lesions, and tracked units showed consistent spiking properties across sessions.Significance: Our findings provide the first evidence that single-neuron recordings can remain stable over the long term following a large hemispheric stroke involving substantial cortical and subcortical injury. They establish the feasibility of chronic, cellular-resolution iBCIs after stroke and support the development of neurorestorative applications for deficits caused by structural brain injury.

articles.title: Non-pharmacological fatigue management strategies in neurodegenerative conditions: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: Fatigue is a common and disabling symptom across several neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. Non-pharmacological strategies are widely used in clinical practice to address fatigue, yet the extent to which evidence from one neurodegenerative condition can inform fatigue management in others remains uncertain, particularly for Parkinson's disease where intervention trials are scarce. To map the quantitative evidence on non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with neurodegenerative diseases (excluding dementias), and to identify potentially transferable strategies, gaps, and priorities for research and practice, with particular relevance to Parkinson's disease. Scoping review conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported using the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF; DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/MJEYP). MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, AMED, and PsycINFO were searched for records published from January 2006 to 15 February 2025. Reference lists of relevant reviews and included studies were screened. Publications in English or Arabic were eligible. Quantitative interventional studies, mixed-methods studies with extractable quantitative fatigue outcomes, and systematic reviews/meta-analyses evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in adults with progressive neurodegenerative conditions were eligible. Conditions of interest included multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, motor neurone disease, Huntington's disease, hereditary ataxias, multiple system atrophy, and progressive supranuclear palsy. Studies focusing solely on pharmacological, surgical, herbal, or homeopathic interventions, qualitative-only studies, and studies in dementias were excluded. A bespoke charting form captured study design, population, intervention, comparator, delivery format, fatigue measures, and key findings. Studies were grouped by intervention type: exercise, psychological, educational, and complementary interventions. Systematic reviews/meta-analyses and primary intervention studies were synthesized as distinct evidence levels and were not combined quantitatively. The search identified 12,618 records. After removal of 5,399 duplicates, 7,219 records were screened and 517 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility. Twenty-seven sources met the inclusion criteria: seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses, 16 randomized controlled trials, one non-randomized controlled study, and three uncontrolled pre-post studies. Evidence was dominated by multiple sclerosis, with only two small trials in Parkinson's disease and no fatigue-focused intervention trials in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. The most consistent between-group benefits were observed for structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management programs in multiple sclerosis. Complementary interventions included acupuncture, light therapy, dietary interventions, and electrical stimulation; evidence across these approaches was mixed. Heterogeneity in intervention type, intensity, duration, supervision and delivery format, follow-up duration, and fatigue outcome measures limited direct comparison across studies. Non-pharmacological interventions for fatigue in neurodegenerative disease are most developed in multiple sclerosis, where structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and educational/self-management approaches show the most consistent benefit. Evidence for Parkinson's disease is sparse, and no fatigue-focused intervention trials were identified in other progressive neurodegenerative conditions. Future work should prioritize condition-specific feasibility and effectiveness studies, harmonized fatigue outcome sets, objective fatigability measures alongside patient-reported fatigue, and multimodal programs with clearly specified therapeutic targets. Fatigue can substantially affect daily life for people living with neurological conditions, but most research on non-drug fatigue management has been conducted in multiple sclerosis. This scoping review mapped 27 sources of evidence on exercise, psychological treatments, education or self-management, and complementary approaches. Structured exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy, and education or self-management showed the most consistent benefits in multiple sclerosis. Only two small fatigue-focused trials were identified in Parkinson’s disease, and no eligible fatigue-focused intervention trials were found in the other progressive neurodegenerative conditions included in the review. Some intervention components, such as pacing, self-monitoring, energy conservation, and graded activity, may be useful across conditions, but they may need adaptation for disease-specific motor, cognitive, autonomic, or progression-related needs. Studies also used many different fatigue measures, and objective fatigability was rarely assessed. Future research should test adapted interventions directly in under-represented conditions and use clearer, more consistent outcome measures.
